scope: Theorem 2.2 (All free-rectangle limits) of the manuscript “BKT universality for height and planar spin fields” (preprints/BKT-universality-for-height-and-planar-spin-fields-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 216 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 5e6a8df09e021c4a), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 13-14. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is a number a = a(k) ∈ [0, k] such that am(k) → a. Let Bn be discrete axis rectangles at mesh n−1 whose endpoints converge to those of a fixed nondegenerate rectangle B. For every finite collection of smooth shifts g on a neighborhood of B, log EBn,k exp{(h, ABn g(·/n))} −→ a 2 Z B |∇g|2 . (2.8) The corresponding tests converge jointly to centered Gaussian variables with covariance a R B ∇g·∇g′; all joint moments converge. For zero-total profiles fn whose scaled piecewise constant densities 13 n2fn converge in L2(B) to a bounded piecewise continuous f of integral zero, the corresponding assertion is log EBn,ke(h,fn) −→ a 2 (f, (−∆B,N )−1 f)L2(B). (2.9) Here the inverse Neumann Laplacian is on integral-zero functions. These statements hold along every such sequence of rectangles and jointly for mixed finite lists of the displayed tests.
